ideas.title: Vibe-Coded App Health Checker
ideas.oneliner: Paste a URL and get a plain-English report on ADA/WCAG gaps, missing privacy policy/cookie banner, broken schema, and demand-letter risk.
ideas.problem: Lovable/Bolt/v0/Cursor produced an explosion of apps from non-devs who ship zero WCAG compliance (4,600+ ADA suits in 2024), no privacy policy, and broken ARIA. They don't find out until a demand letter arrives. Existing checkers (WAVE, axe, Lighthouse) are dev-facing and never cover legal/privacy in plain language.
ideas.who: Hundreds of thousands of indie / no-code builders shipping AI-generated sites; Copper Bay's own client-site audits; Boots students.
ideas.gap: WAVE/axe/Lighthouse/SortSite all exist and are free, but NONE combine accessibility + privacy-policy detection + schema validation + plain-English demand-letter risk framing in one non-technical report. Vibe coders google 'is my website ADA compliant', not 'run axe-core'. The wedge is framing + combined output, not another scanner.
ideas.buildPlan: Serverless fetch on Vercel wraps Lighthouse + public W3C validators + a privacy-policy/cookie-banner string detector + schema.org structured-data check. Output is a single plain-English risk report card, not a dev dump. ~1 week MVP. Paid tier: $9/mo scheduled re-checks via cron/KV.
ideas.notes: Validator KEEP at 79. Only risk: several multi-check free tools (SortSite checks a11y+SEO). Do NOT build another WAVE clone — win entirely on the non-technical legal-risk framing and combined output. Strongest confidence in the set; perfect ProductHunt/Discord/dev-SEO fit ('Is my Lovable app ADA-compliant?' is zero-competition SEO). Build first.

ideas.title: ReserveRight (Winery & Charter edition)
ideas.oneliner: A drop-in deposit-and-hold widget that collects a Stripe deposit and sends reminder texts for wine tastings, tours, and fishing/kayak charters — no platform migration.
ideas.problem: No-shows destroy revenue on time-boxed experiences. OpenTable (TrustPilot 1.4) charges per-cover + $149-499/mo + a new 2% deposit fee and wants to be the primary system; Tock/Resy require full migration. Deposits cut no-shows ~57% but operators can't afford the platform tax.
ideas.who: Sonoma's 425+ wineries and tasting rooms, fishing/kayak charters, cooking classes — Copper Bay's warm local channel.
ideas.gap: The GENERIC restaurant deposit widget is already done well (Carbonara is near-free Stripe pass-through, plus Resmio, Tablein, resOS). But none of these are marketed to wine-country tasting rooms or charter operators, don't appear in wine-tourism contexts, and lack the local trust signal. The defensible niche is winery + charter specifically, sold through Copper Bay's local relationships.
ideas.buildPlan: Static reserve page + Stripe Checkout deposit + Resend/Twilio reminders, embeddable as a <script>. 3-day Vercel build. Monetize through agency relationships from day one; later white-label via Stripe Connect platform account.
needsOwner: FORGE Stripe Connect platform account (white-label/reseller tier)
ideas.notes: Validator RESHAPE 87->78: the 'nobody does bolt-on deposits' claim is false for restaurants (Carbonara undercuts hard). Survives ONLY as the winery/charter niche with the warm local channel as moat. Do not pitch generic restaurants.

ideas.title: Contractor Instant-Quote Page (agency-install)
ideas.oneliner: A done-for-you, pre-configured ballpark-estimate page for a specific trade vertical that qualifies inbound leads before the phone call and emails the contractor pre-filled answers.
ideas.problem: Trades waste ~15 min/call on 'how much for X?' tire-kickers. Field-service suites (Jobber/Housecall, $49-199/mo) force the whole business onto a platform when the real pain is one narrow page.
ideas.who: Plumbers, HVAC, landscapers, electricians, painters — Copper Bay's core trades client base in Sonoma County.
ideas.gap: Generic DIY quote-widget builders already exist and are free (CalcWidget, ConvertCalculator, CALCONIC, QuoteIQ). So the build-your-own SaaS angle is dead. The surviving wedge is 'we set it up for you for your trade and you own it' — an agency-delivered product, not a self-serve builder.
ideas.buildPlan: JSON-driven question tree -> ballpark range -> lead email via Resend, delivered as a pre-built embed snippet per trade. 2-day build. Sold as a fixed-fee agency setup + small monthly hosting/support, not a SaaS subscription.
ideas.notes: Validator RESHAPE 84->74: free incumbents own the builder lane, so the 'no standalone qualifier exists' gap is false. Compete on done-for-you install + ownership through the Copper Bay channel, not features. Natural bundle with the Job-Completion Report into a trades stack.

ideas.title: Marina Slip Waitlist & Day-Use Lite
ideas.oneliner: A lightweight public waitlist plus day-use launch reservation page with deposit collection for small marinas and county boat launches.
ideas.problem: Roughly 73% of small marinas (directional) run on spreadsheets; Dockwa/DockMaster/PayMyDock ($99-500/mo) are built for full-service marinas with fuel docks. County launches still mail PDF forms. Nobody serves the sub-10-slip / launch / outfitter operator's single pain.
ideas.who: Sub-50-slip marinas, county park boat launches, yacht clubs, kayak/SUP outfitters.
ideas.gap: Snag-A-Slip (free-to-list, pay-per-booking) is the closest threat but is a marketplace model, not a self-hosted waitlist widget. PayMyDock/MARINAGO/MarinaOffice are over-built 80-feature suites. Nothing affordable serves only waitlist + day-use for the smallest operators.
ideas.buildPlan: Calendar + form + Stripe deposit + Resend confirmation. 3-4 day Vercel build. Dog-food at Lake Sonoma Marina first as the flagship reference, then replicate. Build the minimum Lake Sonoma actually needs; do not over-engineer.
ideas.notes: Validator KEEP at 73. Moat is the live seed client + Copper Bay local network, not the software. Complements the existing marina SaaS. Note: Stripe+Resend are server-side keys, so Vercel free (not GitHub Pages).

ideas.title: Job-Completion Report + Review Push
ideas.oneliner: Tech snaps before/after photos and the customer gets a branded PDF of what was done plus a one-tap Google-review CTA while the goodwill is fresh.
ideas.problem: CompanyCam ($79-199/mo, 3-user min) is photo-only; ServiceTitan/Jobber/Housecall bury photos inside $50-150+/user suites. Nobody owns the customer-facing 'completion moment' that both prevents disputes and harvests reviews.
ideas.who: Roofers, painters, HVAC, plumbers — Copper Bay's trades base.
ideas.gap: Photo apps are standalone and dev/internal-facing; suites treat photos as a secondary feature; none close the customer-facing review loop with a branded completion report. The 'completion moment' is genuinely unoccupied.
ideas.buildPlan: PWA camera + Cloudinary upload + client-side PDF + public report URL + Google-review deep link. Realistically 3-4 weeks to an MVP that works reliably on iOS Safari (camera/upload complexity is non-trivial).
ideas.notes: Validator KEEP at 71 (trimmed from 73 for iOS PWA build complexity — '1-2 weeks' was optimistic). Natural bundle with the trades quote page into a Copper Bay trades stack.

ideas.title: Local GEO Audit (agency lead magnet)
ideas.oneliner: Enter a business name and location to get a report card on AI-Overview citation, LocalBusiness JSON-LD validity, and NAP consistency — as a free Copper Bay lead magnet.
ideas.problem: AI Overviews now hit ~25.8% of US searches and local businesses are anxious about being invisible to AI search. Paid GEO tools (Goodie, Scrunch, SE Ranking) are generalist and $49-199/mo.
ideas.who: Local businesses worried about AI-search visibility, and the agency (Copper Bay) that pitches them.
ideas.gap: A crowded free tier is already emerging (Blazly GEO free, GEO Metrics, others) for AI-visibility checks, so the standalone-product gap is closing. But the genuinely zero-secret slice — client-side JSON-LD + NAP validation as a free explainer that funnels to a 'book a GEO audit with us' CTA — is a clean distribution asset for the agency.
ideas.buildPlan: Static one-page explainer + client-side JSON-LD/schema validator + NAP consistency check (genuinely zero-secret) + manual 'book a GEO audit' CTA. 1-2 days. The live AI-Overview citation check needs a SerpAPI/Serper key and is a later paid add.
needsOwner: SerpAPI/Serper (only for the live AI-Overview citation tier later)
ideas.notes: Validator RESHAPE 79->65: as a standalone GEO SaaS it's CUT (free tier already crowded, and the meaningful AI-citation check is NOT zero-secret). Survives as a free agency lead-magnet + funnel, not a product.

ideas.title: Review-Pulse (white-label add-on)
ideas.oneliner: A QR/link micro-app that routes happy customers to a Google review and unhappy ones to private feedback — sold as a configured, agency-branded add-on, not a standalone SaaS.
ideas.problem: Birdeye starts $299/mo (with BBB billing-trap complaints) and Podium $249-599 — priced for franchises, locking out solo operators who still desperately want more Google reviews.
ideas.who: Single-location local businesses already on Copper Bay's roster — restaurants, salons, contractors, marinas.
ideas.gap: The cheap standalone lane is saturated (WiserReview $9/mo, Reputigo $14.95/mo, OpenWidget free, NiceJob, GatherUp), and the experience-gate pattern is a standard feature, not a differentiator. There is no room to win on price as a new standalone SaaS. The only viable angle is bundling a configured instance as a white-label add-on resold with agency branding + support.
ideas.buildPlan: Static page + public Google Maps review deep-link + sentiment fork; no API keys for the MVP. 1-2 days. Resell as a configured ~$29/mo agency add-on (or fold into the trades stack as a feature), not a new branded product.
ideas.notes: Validator RESHAPE 82->65: too crowded at $9-15 to win on price as standalone. Either resell an existing tool (WiserReview/Reputigo) white-label or ship as a bundled feature of the Copper Bay trades stack — do not build/market a fresh standalone SaaS.
